$Comment: The Blight Warden's fight, run by the game's own encounter scripts. The round stands this script
up at the Heartwood Gate the moment the last shrine is lit; the script raises the Warden, runs
its three phases and its adds, and tells the Ziggfreed Common library every beat through the zc:
signals, which is how the gate opens, how the party's health scale and credit work, and how the
notices in Server/ZiggfreedCommon/FeedbackMoments/KweebecNightmare_Warden_*.json fire. What the
server owes for the fight (the party scale, the notices, the map marker) is the binding row
Server/ZiggfreedCommon/Encounters/KweebecNightmare_Warden_Encounter.json; nothing about the fight itself
is written anywhere but here and in the three Warden roles.
The shape follows Ziggfreed Common's Zc_Encounter_Base and adds the phase states the base leaves
to a script of its own. The first three instructions run every tick beside whatever state the
fight is in: the Player sensor keeps the roster the boss bar, the scale and the credit read;
TriggerSpawners raises the Warden from the KweebecNightmare_Warden_Marker spawn marker while
the fight is in Intro and no boss is bound yet (the round stamps that marker and the four
Blight markers into the ground at the gate as blocks when the grove is built, so the markers are
already standing here); and the release, on the Target sensor alone, makes the Warden
vulnerable, puts the bar up under its name, sends zc:engaged and moves into Phase_1. The
release keys on the bound boss and never on a beacon, so the Warden role does not have to send
one.
Intro also carries the fight's one safety net: if no Warden has bound within the Timeout below
(twenty seconds; a missing marker, a role that failed to load), the script sends
zc:kweebec:no_show and retires to Complete, and the round opens the gate rather than leave the
party barred behind a boss that never came. The countdown stops the instant a boss binds.
The phases. Phase_1 is the Warden as spawned. At half its health it sheds its bark: the role
changes in place to KweebecNightmare_Warden_Phase2 (the engine keeps its aggro, its target
slot and its current health across the change; only the maximum re-rolls), zc:phase:Phase_2
goes out, and the first wave of two Blighted Kweebec rises from the Blight markers. At half of
what it carried into Phase_2 it changes to KweebecNightmare_Warden_Phase3, wreathed in fire,
with a wave of three. Each phase role's MaxHealth is authored as the health the Warden carries
into that phase, so the bar reads full at every phase start and the three phases together add
up to the first role's 600; retune the first role to lengthen the whole fight, retune
HealthRange here to move where the phases begin. Count on the waves is how many Blight markers
fire; a marker whose spawn is still alive does not fire again, so four stamped markers cap the
live adds at four however the waves fall.
The defeat beat sits in every phase, because the Warden can fall in any of them: when the Target
sensor loses the boss the bar comes down, the slot is released, zc:defeated goes out and the
script retires to Complete. The library settles the credit the instant the death lands, so the
beat here is the authoritative place the bar comes down. Complete is terminal on purpose: the
round world is torn down seconds after the fight, so there is nothing to re-arm for and a
second fight would only be noise.
Every Target sensor reaches 256 blocks from the encounter entity at the gate, which covers the
whole grove: the Warden hunts wherever the party runs and must never drop out of the fight for
being far from where it rose. There is no fight music here; the round already keeps its own
dread bed playing on every survivor's client.
Override this file by id from your own pack to change the fight for every server, or retune
the Warden roles under Server/NPC/Roles/KweebecNightmare for the numbers alone. Keep the file
name distinct from every NPC role's: an encounter script and a role share one id namespace, and
a script named after a role replaces that role at load.
